regions.name: Middle East
overview: The US-Israel-Iran war has crossed from bilateral exchange into a genuine multi-front regional war — Iranian retaliation struck US bases in Kuwait and Bahrain, missiles again targeted Jordan's Aqaba, and a drone attack on Egypt's Damietta port marks the first strike on Egyptian soil, all while Washington and Israel weigh a further large-scale strike on Iran's energy infrastructure as soon as this weekend.

Saudi Arabia has become the region's central actor rather than a bystander — simultaneously absorbing direct Houthi strikes on Aramco's Jizan and Abqaiq infrastructure, joining US airstrikes against Iran-backed militias in Iraq, and formally launching a 14-nation Maritime Defense Alliance, placing Riyadh at the intersection of nearly every active flashpoint from the Red Sea to the Gulf.

Diplomacy and violence are running on parallel, disconnected tracks in the Palestinian theater — even as the Hamas-Board of Peace disarmament agreement was hailed as a 'historic breakthrough' on 30 July, Israeli strikes killed Palestinians in Gaza the very next day and the West Bank remains under near-lockdown with UN-declared settler violence at an all-time high.

All three of the region's critical maritime chokepoints are now simultaneously contested — Hormuz traffic has collapsed to a fraction of pre-war volume, the Bab el-Mandeb remains under a declared Houthi blockade, and the Suez Canal faces steep new war-risk surcharges — with Iraq's Iran-aligned militias signaling further escalation once the Arbaeen pilgrimage concludes on 6 August.

countries.name: Gaza
incidents: 30 Jul — Washington/Gaza: The Board of Peace announced Hamas agreed to a phased disarmament deal; police weapons surrendered first, heavy-weapons and tunnel decommissioning could take 200-350 days, contingent on Israeli withdrawal.
1 Aug — Sheikh Radwan, Gaza City: An Israeli strike killed 2 Palestinians the day after the disarmament announcement; the cumulative toll since the Oct 2025 ceasefire reached 1,222.
1 Aug — Deir al-Balah: An Israeli strike destroyed two medicine-storage warehouses beside Al-Aqsa Martyrs Hospital.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. The 30 Jul disarmament breakthrough and the lethal strikes that followed it within 24 hours confirm the ceasefire and battlefield tracks remain disconnected. Expect the 14-day drafting deadline for the disarmament roadmap (mid-August) to become the next flashpoint, with continued Israeli strikes at reduced but persistent tempo and Hamas conditioning further steps on visible withdrawal. Spoiler action from hardline factions on both sides is a material risk before the first verification milestones are reached.

countries.name: Lebanon
incidents: 10 Jul — Kfarrumman, Nabatieh district: Israeli drone strikes on a motorcycle and car killed one and wounded three.
28 Jul — Nabatieh al-Fawqa: Israeli drones struck an apartment complex, causing substantial damage and fire.
30-31 Jul — Beaufort area, south Lebanon: The IDF announced it destroyed a two-decade-old Iran-funded Hezbollah tunnel network, describing it as dismantling an underground stronghold.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. Israel's systematic dismantlement of Hezbollah's remaining tunnel and rocket infrastructure continues under the ceasefire-enforcement rationale, testing Beirut's tolerance without a mass-casualty flashpoint this week. Risk of a sharper Hezbollah response rises if strikes expand into central Beirut proper, or if a degraded Iran looks to Hezbollah to open a new pressure front amid its own widening confrontation with the US.

countries.name: Iran
incidents: 29-30 Jul — Qeshm Island/Ahvaz/Abadan: The US conducted a 'heavy wave' of strikes on dozens of IRGC targets across southern Iran; a family was killed in a residential building on Qeshm.
30-31 Jul — Kuwait/Bahrain: Iran's army claimed drone strikes on the US's Ahmad Al Jaber Air Base in Kuwait and Sheikh Isa Air Base in Bahrain, framed as retaliation for the Qeshm strike.
31 Jul — Camp David: The Trump administration weighed a further 'heavy' wave of strikes on Iran's energy infrastructure; some aides reportedly opposed, no final decision yet.
Ongoing — Strait of Hormuz: Shipping traffic collapsed from roughly 130 ships/day pre-war to a handful, reflecting the scale of disruption.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained; trajectory toward further escalation. US and Israeli officials are reportedly preparing a large-scale strike on Iran's energy infrastructure as soon as this weekend. Expect any new strike wave to trigger further Iranian retaliation against US basing across the Gulf (Kuwait, Bahrain, Qatar) and against Jordan/Saudi Arabia, with the Senate's rejection of the War Powers resolution removing a near-term domestic constraint on Washington.

countries.name: Yemen
incidents: 20 Jul — Nationwide: Houthis declared a maritime blockade of Saudi Arabia.
25 Jul — Yemen (Houthi-held areas): The Saudi-led coalition struck Houthi military targets in retaliation for tanker attacks.
28 Jul — Red Sea: Houthis claimed missile strikes on Saudi tankers Encelia and Layla, sparking fires on both vessels — the first attacks since the blockade declaration.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. Sustained tanker attacks, a declared blockade and direct Saudi retaliatory strikes confirm continued high-intensity conflict, with oil prices briefly topping $100/barrel. Expect continued Houthi harassment of Saudi-linked shipping and further exchanges inside Yemen; a sustained blockade risks drawing the newly formalized 14-nation Maritime Defense Alliance into direct enforcement action.

countries.name: Israel
incidents: 30 Jul — West Bank-wide: UN OCHA declared settler violence at an 'all-time high' — 18 Palestinians killed by settlers in 2026 so far, versus 17 in all of 2025.
31 Jul — Tal village, West Bank: Israeli forces shot and wounded a Palestinian, arrested 3, and sealed village entrances as 100+ settlers marched in under IDF escort.
31 Jul — Juniad neighborhood, Nablus: 11 Palestinians, including 4 children, were injured in a settler-and-soldier raid.

Ongoing — West Bank-wide: Curfews and closures since the 24 Jul violence remain in place across Nablus, Ramallah and Bethlehem, with movement obstacles now numbering 925, a 43% increase severely disrupting ambulance access.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. The UN's 'all-time high' characterization and continued near-daily incidents confirm sustained critical-level unrest. Expect settler violence and IDF operations to remain mutually reinforcing, with closures likely to persist or tighten further, especially if backlash from the Gaza disarmament process emerges among Israeli hardliners opposed to withdrawal.

countries.name: Iraq
incidents: 27 Jul — Erbil/Mosul area: KRG PM Masrour Barzani accused Iran-aligned militias near Mosul of targeting Erbil with drones.

29-30 Jul — Baghdad, Wasit, Nineveh, Basra, Kirkuk, Karbala, Diyala: US and Saudi forces conducted joint strikes on Iran-backed PMF sites following 30+ militia drone attacks in 72 hours, killing roughly 20 fighters and 6 Iranian advisers.
30 Jul — Baghdad: PM al-Zaidi ordered 'maximum' alert readiness across Iraqi military and PMF bases.

30 Jul — Nationwide: Kataib Sayyid al-Shuhada and Kataib Hezbollah vowed 'inevitable' retaliation against US and Saudi interests, with the 'Islamic Resistance in Iraq' stating its response will follow the Arbaeen pilgrimage's conclusion on 6 August.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained; imminent flashpoint identified. High confidence of a significant Iran-aligned militia attack on US or Saudi interests shortly after 6 August, timed to avoid disrupting Arbaeen. This will likely trigger a further round of US-Saudi strikes, continuing the escalatory cycle; Baghdad's control over militia elements remains doubtful despite the alert order.

countries.name: Saudi Arabia
incidents: 25 Jul — Yemen border region: The Saudi-led coalition struck Houthi targets in retaliation for tanker attacks.

28 Jul — Red Sea/Jizan/Abqaiq: Houthi missile strikes hit tankers Encelia and Layla; the Jizan refinery (400,000 bpd) remains shut until mid-August, and satellite imagery shows damage to an Abqaiq processing train.
29-30 Jul — Iraq: Saudi Arabia joined US strikes on Iran-backed militias, killing roughly 20 fighters and 6 Iranian advisers.

31 Jul — Riyadh: Saudi Arabia formally launched the 14-nation Maritime Defense Alliance, with officials from 43 countries and the EU joining talks to protect Red Sea, Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb shipping.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. Riyadh continues its dual-track posture of retaliatory strikes against Houthi and militia targets alongside coalition-building, while remaining exposed to further attacks on Aramco infrastructure; the Jizan outage through mid-August will pressure regional fuel supply. The formalized Maritime Defense Alliance marks Saudi Arabia's clearest move yet toward institutionalizing a regional security response.

countries.name: Syria
incidents: Jul (ongoing) — Aleppo/Azaz/Al-Bab: Syria's Interior Ministry continued arrests of suspected ISIS-cell members in joint operations.
Through Jul — Nationwide: SOHR recorded 5 ISIS attacks in July, killing 3, bringing the 2026 total to 64 attacks — consistent with the sustained monthly tempo tracked since spring.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained, though this week's confirmed new activity was limited to the routine monthly ISIS tally rather than a new mass-casualty event — worth flagging for a possible downgrade to HIGH if this pattern holds. Expect continued low-level ISIS cell activity at a roughly steady rate absent a major counter-ISIS operation; Syria's neutral posture in the Iran-US war remains intact but increasingly tested as the war's footprint widens into Iraq, Jordan, Kuwait, Bahrain and Egypt.

countries.name: Egypt
incidents: 29 Jul — Damietta port: A drone strike ignited fires on the US-owned LNG carrier Energos Winter and the Greek-owned GasLog Salem — the first attack on Egyptian soil since the war began; no casualties, Iran and the Houthis both deny responsibility.

30-31 Jul — Suez Canal Authority: Further war-risk surcharge hikes were announced (crude/product tankers 25%→37%, LNG carriers 7%→19%, dry bulk 10%→22%) as London's marine-insurance market widened its high-risk zone.
31 Jul — Cairo: President Sisi warned of 'the danger of regional escalation' following the Damietta strike.
countries.coa: Upgraded to CRITICAL from HIGH. The Damietta strike is the first confirmed attack on sovereign Egyptian territory since the war began, a threshold crossing regardless of the absence of casualties. Expect tightened port and Canal security, continued surcharge increases, and further reduced Suez traffic if attribution remains unresolved; a repeat attack — especially one causing casualties — would sharply raise the threat picture further and could force a formal Egyptian military response.

countries.name: Jordan
incidents: 22-23 Jul — Aqaba: Iran launched missiles and drones at Aqaba port and airport; Jordanian forces intercepted six missiles and four drones.
29-30 Jul — Aqaba: A renewed Iranian strike targeted the port city; Jordan's Foreign Ministry summoned Iran's charge d'affaires and lodged a formal protest.
30 Jul — Jordanian airspace: Air defenses intercepted 5 further Iranian missiles with no casualties in Jordan.
31 Jul — Amman: Jordan joined the newly announced 14-nation Saudi-led Maritime Defense Alliance.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. Jordan remains a frequent target and transit corridor for Iranian strikes aimed at US and Israeli-adjacent interests, with continued interception events around Aqaba given its proximity to Eilat and US regional logistics. Jordan's participation in the new maritime coalition signals deepening security alignment with Riyadh and Washington, which may itself invite further Iranian pressure.

countries.name: Libya
incidents: 12 Jul — Gatrun, southern Libya: A newly self-proclaimed rebel group, the 'Southern Liberation Operations Room,' attacked a Libyan National Army checkpoint.
20 Jul — Eastern Libya: Turkey expanded military and technical cooperation with Haftar's LNA.
25 Jul — Tripoli and other cities: Protests erupted over power cuts and heatwave-driven electricity shortages.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. No new independently verified incidents were identified for the past week; Libya's trajectory remains one of political consolidation under Haftar aided by deepening Turkish engagement, combined with rising civil unrest over basic services. Expect continued Tripoli-area protests over power and utilities through the summer heat season, with the Gatrun checkpoint attack still worth monitoring as a marginal new armed challenger in the south.

countries.name: Tunisia
incidents: 4 & 8 Jul — Tunis: Courts convicted and sentenced Ennahda leaders, including a 14-year in-absentia sentence for Rached Ghannouchi.

25 Jul — Tunis: Thousands rallied on Habib Bourguiba Avenue demanding President Saied's resignation, marking the 5th anniversary of his 2021 emergency-powers self-coup; organizers noted the protest base has expanded beyond traditional opposition.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. Protests remain large but non-violent, with continued 'simmering' public anger beneath an outwardly calm political surface. Ennahda leadership remains imprisoned, limiting organized opposition capacity; expect continued periodic mass protests around symbolic dates without a near-term shift toward violent unrest, though watch for any hardening of state response if protest momentum builds further.

regions.name: Ukraine/Russia
overview: Russia's deepening self-inflicted energy crisis — fuel shortages in 78 of 83 regions, reportedly reaching military units — is colliding with record-scale missile/drone barrages on Kyiv three days running, including a Polish-airspace incursion, suggesting Moscow is racing to break Ukrainian resolve before its own economic base fractures further.

Moscow is running near-identical coercive economic playbooks against Armenia (trade bans expanded beyond dairy) and Moldova's Transnistria (a tenfold citizenship-fee hike), even as both governments respond by accelerating their EU pivot rather than retreating from it.

Domestic legitimacy strain is compounding external pressure region-wide — Ukraine's Fedorov protests now overlap with an acknowledged Patriot-interceptor shortage, Georgia's 610-day protest movement collides with a suspected sabotage attack on national infrastructure, and Azerbaijan's 12-15-year sentences against journalists signal governments choosing control over accommodation.

The Belarus-Baltic frontier is hardening in parallel with the main war — Latvia's looming state of emergency (11 Aug-10 Nov) and Lithuania's border-control debate, layered onto Minsk's continued special-forces buildup opposite Ukraine — keeping the tri-border zone a plausible site for accidental escalation.

countries.name: Ukraine
incidents: 30 Jul — Nationwide: Russia launched 70+ missiles and roughly 280 drones overnight, striking as far west as Lviv; a missile crossed into Polish airspace, prompting NATO to scramble Polish jets; at least 8-10 were killed.

31 Jul — Kyiv: Russia struck the capital again with ballistic missiles and drones, the second major attack in 48 hours, killing several and wounding over a dozen; a residential building partially collapsed.

1 Aug — Kyiv: Russia launched 35 missiles (27 ballistic) and 185 Shahed-type drones, mostly aimed at the capital; 9 were killed and 23 injured. Zelensky said only one ballistic missile was intercepted 'because there are no missiles for the Patriots.'
Ongoing through 31 Jul — Nationwide: Protests demanding Fedorov's reinstatement continued past their 10th day; Fedorov reaffirmed he will accept no post short of defense minister.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained, compounding. Three major missile/drone barrages on Kyiv in three consecutive days, combined with an explicit admission of depleted Patriot interceptor stock, mark a compounding rather than de-escalating trajectory. Expect Russia to sustain or increase strike tempo through autumn while exploiting the acknowledged air-defense shortage, with Western scrambling to backfill interceptors and continued risk of further NATO airspace incursions. The unresolved Fedorov standoff is likely to persist as chronic low-boil unrest, with continued battlefield strain raising the risk of further high-level command reshuffles.

countries.name: Russia
incidents: 30 Jul — Novorossiysk: A drone struck the tanker Nissos Sifnos loading Tengizchevroil crude at CPC's SPM-3 mooring, again suspending loading on a route carrying roughly 80% of Kazakhstan's oil exports.

31 Jul — Volgograd Oblast: Ukrainian drones hit the Lukoil-Volgogradneftepererabotka refinery (15 million ton/year capacity, one of Russia's largest) and a logistics hub, killing at least 1; parallel strikes hit the TAIF-NK refinery in Tatarstan, an aircraft plant, the port of Taman and an EW system.

Ongoing — Nationwide: The fuel crisis now affects 78 of 83 regions plus occupied Crimea; six regions report complete gasoline shortages, crude processing is down to 3.91M bpd (roughly 1.4M bpd below last year), and shortages are reportedly reaching army units directly.
countries.coa: Upgraded to CRITICAL from HIGH. Ukrainian strikes have now hit a second major refinery complex (Volgograd) on top of continued CPC tanker attacks, and the fuel crisis has expanded from a regional nuisance to a near-nationwide phenomenon reportedly reaching military logistics — a materially different scale than late July. Expect Ukraine to continue prioritizing refinery, tanker and logistics-hub strikes as an economic-pressure campaign, with rising risk the fuel crisis begins constraining Russian military resupply and showing up as slowed offensive tempo.

countries.name: Belarus
incidents: 22 Jul — Belarus-Ukraine border: Lukashenko confirmed Special Operations Forces dispersal along the border, framed as defensive, amid continued military infrastructure construction.
Mid-Jul — Latvia-Belarus border: Migratory pressure increased sharply, with roughly 8,000 illegal crossing attempts recorded by mid-July.
Late Jul — Riga: Latvia announced a state of emergency along its 175km Belarus border from 11 Aug to 10 Nov, authorizing military and police use of force to push back migrants.
Late Jul — Vilnius: Lithuania reported a fourfold rise in secondary migration from Latvia (300 to 1,200 cases in H1 2026) and is weighing temporary border controls.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. The core dynamic — Lukashenko avoiding direct war involvement while running a migrant-pressure campaign — is unchanged, but Latvia's looming emergency declaration and Lithuania's border-control debate mark an incremental hardening of the Baltic response. Expect the migrant-pressure campaign to intensify through autumn as Latvia's measures take effect, likely triggering reciprocal Belarusian rhetoric, while continued SOF positioning near the Ukraine border warrants monitoring for any shift toward offensive posture.

countries.name: Moldova
incidents: 21-22 Jul — Chișinău: The Tofan government was sworn in, naming EU accession its top priority.
22-31 Jul — Bucharest: PM Tofan stated he would support Moldova-Romania unification if put to referendum and met Romanian-Moldovan diaspora, a notable rhetorical escalation.
22-24 Jul — Moscow: Russia raised the consular fee for Transnistria residents' Russian citizenship applications nearly tenfold ($84.5 to $780), reversing a May decree that had simplified access.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. This week's developments were largely political and diplomatic rather than security-driven, with no confirmed Transnistria military-posture escalation. Watch whether Tofan's unification remarks provoke a sharper Russian or Transnistrian response given Moscow's pattern of framing Chișinău's moves as provocations; the citizenship fee hike may signal Moscow recalibrating rather than escalating its Transnistria leverage.

countries.name: Georgia
incidents: 24-25 Jul — Tbilisi/Batumi/Kutaisi/Kobuleti/Telavi: Two nationwide blackouts hit multiple cities; the State Security Service opened a sabotage investigation under critical-infrastructure statutes after Tbilisi Metro trains stalled in tunnels requiring evacuation.

26-27 Jul — Tbilisi: 10 people were detained for anti-Ivanishvili posters outside City Hall; activist Nodar Tsitsriashvili was separately detained in Freedom Square for a similar poster; court proceedings later handed down administrative detentions and fines.
30 Jul — Tbilisi: Pro-EU protests reached their 610th consecutive day on Rustaveli Avenue.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained, trending toward the upper end. The combination of suspected sabotage against national critical infrastructure and a deepening crackdown on dissent — including a new Interior Ministry 'hate speech department' that has drawn US Embassy concern — marks a qualitative escalation beyond routine protest policing. Expect continued daily low-level detentions tied to the 600+ day protest movement; if the blackout sabotage is formally attributed to a hostile actor, expect a sharp shift in government rhetoric and potentially further crackdown measures justified on national-security grounds.

countries.name: Armenia
incidents: 27 Jul — Moscow/Yerevan: Russia's dairy import ban took effect as scheduled; Pashinyan personally appealed to Putin, calling the measure politicized.
29 Jul — Yerevan: Pashinyan declared the EAEU 'paralyzed and not functioning,' warning of 'the beginning of the end' for the bloc absent resolution.
Late Jul — Moscow: Russia expanded restrictions beyond dairy to flowers, mineral water, vegetables and fruit, timed with Armenia's election preparations.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained, trending toward HIGH. Russia's broadening of trade bans into multiple agricultural categories, paired with Pashinyan's unusually blunt 'paralyzed' characterization of the EAEU, signals an accelerating and more overt economic-coercion campaign. Expect further Russian trade restrictions ahead of Armenia's parliamentary elections, testing whether Yerevan's EU pivot survives sustained pressure; a Moody's outlook upgrade to positive offers a partial counter-signal.

countries.name: Azerbaijan
incidents: 13 Jul — Shusha: President Aliyev said Azerbaijan is 'unequivocally considering' full withdrawal from the Council of Europe, a threat that remains unresolved as the CoE Secretary General has reportedly asked Baku to reconsider.
27-31 Jul — Baku: Nine journalists and activists in the 'Toplum TV' case were sentenced to 12-15 years in prison, drawing international rights-group protests as a major press-freedom crackdown.
Late Jul — Baku: A French citizen's 10-year espionage conviction was upheld on appeal.
countries.coa: Upgraded to MODERATE from LOW. The scale of the Toplum TV sentencing is a significant domestic-repression escalation, even without direct regional security implications, combined with the unresolved Council of Europe withdrawal threat. Expect Azerbaijan's formal decision on CoE withdrawal to be a notable geopolitical signal to watch; continued harsh sentencing of journalists is likely to draw further international criticism but is unlikely to alter Baku's trajectory given its strengthened negotiating position with both Russia and the West.

regions.name: Sahel
overview: State-aligned and foreign-backed forces are increasingly co-implicated in civilian harm alongside insurgent violence — Russia's Africa Corps faces fresh HRW allegations of an indiscriminate air strike in Mali's Mopti region, while Sudan's own army escalates retaliatory airstrikes in Kordofan even as RSF conducts reprisal massacres — complicating any simple government-versus-insurgent framing.

Militant and criminal networks are demonstrating deepening cross-border coordination and scale — from JNIM-FLA's joint offensives in Mali and JNIM-ISSP rivalry spilling across Niger and Burkina Faso, to Nigeria's Zamfara-Katsina bandit networks now mounting 200-plus-fighter assaults and abducting local officials.

The human toll is increasingly measured in mass displacement and maritime tragedy, not just battlefield casualties — Mauritania's confirmed deadliest 2026 migration disaster, Sudan's North Kordofan reprisal-driven displacement, and continued flight into Chad collectively outpace regional humanitarian response capacity.

External security realignments are proceeding but have yet to translate into battlefield results — Chad's rapprochement with France and Mali's deepening reliance on Russia's Africa Corps both represent significant strategic pivots, yet neither has meaningfully blunted insurgent operational tempo this quarter.

countries.name: Mali
incidents: 18 Jul — Anefis/Tabankort: A joint JNIM-FLA ambush on a FAMa-Africa Corps convoy killed 50+ personnel.
31 Jul (dated 15 Jun, surfaced this week) — Kyrnia village, Mopti region: HRW accused Russia's Africa Corps of an 'indiscriminate' air strike that killed 8 civilians, including 3 children.

25-26 Jul — Niono/Ségou region: FAMa and Africa Corps forces expanded Operation Dougoukoloko, claiming to strike JNIM/FLA hideouts and fallback bases; a JNIM fuel and road blockade around Bamako, in place since early July, continued.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. Fresh HRW allegations against Africa Corps add a second axis of violence — state-aligned forces harming civilians — on top of the 18 Jul Anefis mass-casualty ambush. Expect continued JNIM-FLA pressure on FAMa-Africa Corps convoys in the Gao-Kidal corridor and persistent economic pressure on Bamako via blockades, while Africa Corps' expanding air campaign is likely to generate further credible civilian-harm allegations, feeding both jihadist recruitment and diplomatic friction.

countries.name: Niger
incidents: 17 Jul — Téra, Tillabéri region: 16 Nigerien soldiers were killed and 23 wounded in a militant attack near the tri-border zone.
31 Jul — N'Guigmi, Diffa Region: A coordinated attack and follow-on ambush killed at least 14 Nigerien security personnel near a National Guard position.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. The N'Guigmi attack follows the 17 Jul Téra attack as a second mass-casualty security-forces incident in two weeks, sustaining a high operational tempo even where no additional incidents were independently confirmed this week. Niger's forces remain stretched across two active fronts — JNIM/FLA pressure from the west and a resurgent Boko Haram/ISWAP push from the southeast — with further coordinated multi-site attacks likely.

countries.name: Burkina Faso
incidents: 28 Jul — Gorom Gorom, Sahel region: ISSP attacked a humanitarian convoy carrying aid to the besieged town, killing at least 9 civilians.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. No new dated incident was confirmed this week beyond the Gorom Gorom convoy attack, likely reflecting reporting and access constraints in jihadist-blockaded zones rather than a genuine lull — actual incident tempo is probably higher than open sources currently confirm. Expect continued ISSP and JNIM targeting of humanitarian access routes and besieged towns.

countries.name: Sudan
incidents: 27 Jul — El Obeid: RSF drone strikes hit two municipal buildings at dawn, in apparent retaliation after SAF regained control of the Khartoum-El Obeid highway.
29 Jul — Jammama, North Kordofan: An RSF attack killed 9 civilians and wounded 14 after residents were accused of collaborating with SAF; the market and health center were looted.

29 Jul — Um Badr, Sodari, Abu Zaima, Hamrat al-Sheikh, El Mazroub: RSF units retreating from North Kordofan launched further retaliatory raids — looting, home raids and arrests of residents accused of aiding SAF.
30 Jul — North Kordofan: IOM reported over 1,400 people newly displaced following the RSF attacks; SAF launched heavy retaliatory airstrikes on RSF positions.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained, escalating. RSF's pattern of retreat-triggered reprisals against civilians has spread across five-plus North Kordofan towns, combined with SAF counter-strikes, raising the risk of El Obeid replicating the El Fasher siege/atrocity dynamic. Expect North Kordofan to consolidate as Sudan's next major atrocity flashpoint, with accelerating displacement into Chad and within Sudan straining an already-overwhelmed humanitarian response.

countries.name: Chad
incidents: 20-22 Jul — Kalbus/Al-Tina, West Darfur border: An RSF drone strike on Al-Tina town killed and injured civilians and military personnel, with explosions and airstrikes heard from refugee camps inside Chad.

28-30 Jul — N'Djamena: Chad and France confirmed a new military-cooperation framework — small, flexible teams for training, intelligence-sharing and air support without permanent bases — the first concrete step since Chad terminated its 2024 defense pact with France.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. No new cross-border incident was confirmed this week, a mild positive signal, but continued SAF/RSF/Joint Force reinforcement near the border sustains elevated risk. Chad's re-engagement with France signals hedging against both RSF spillover from Darfur and Boko Haram/ISWAP pressure in the Lake Chad basin, though the 'no permanent bases' framework limits how quickly it can reinforce eastern border defenses.

countries.name: Mauritania
incidents: 14-18 Jul — Off Nouadhibou: A vessel carrying roughly 180 migrants from The Gambia was found after 25 days at sea with 143 dead or missing and only 38 survivors — the deadliest single Atlantic-route incident of 2026, part of a broader toll of 144 confirmed dead or missing that week.
Ongoing — Nouadhibou/Nouakchott: UNHCR recorded 17 disembarkations and 2,147 people rescued off Mauritania's coast so far in 2026.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. No newly dated maritime incident was found within this specific week, but the confirmed scale of the 14-18 Jul disaster — the year's deadliest migration tragedy — underscores continuing structural risk. Expect continued high-volume, high-risk Atlantic route departures toward the Canaries, with Mauritanian Coast Guard capacity likely to remain overwhelmed relative to traffic volume absent expanded rescue coordination with Spain/EU assets.

countries.name: Nigeria
incidents: 25 Jul — Zango, Bungudu LGA, Zamfara: Bandits stormed the residence of a local government chairman, killing 2 police officers and 2 vigilantes and abducting the chairman and his family.
26 Jul — Magami Dantoro village, Kaura Namoda LGA, Zamfara: A bandit attack killed 1 and injured 1, with property looted.
26-27 Jul — Guga village, Bakori LGA, Katsina: 200+ bandits attacked the village but were repelled by Hunters and Community Watch Corps; 40+ bandits, including senior commanders, were killed.
Ongoing — Lassa, Borno: The 36 students and 1 staff member abducted 29-30 Jun remain in Boko Haram captivity a month on.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. The scale of the Katsina attack (200+ attackers) and evident Zamfara-Katsina bandit-network coordination indicate growing organizational sophistication rather than de-escalation, with the Bungudu abduction showing bandits directly targeting local government officials. Community defense forces are showing tactical success repelling large assaults, but the shift toward abducting officials signals adaptation to pressure; the Lassa students remain at meaningful risk of extended captivity absent a negotiated release or decisive rescue operation.

regions.name: Asia-Pacific
overview: South China Sea presence has crossed from gray-zone friction to great-power military signaling — the arrival of the USS George Washington carrier strike group off the Philippines, layered on the Scarborough/Second Thomas Shoal clashes and a public PLA rebuke, marks the clearest US military counter-signal of the summer.

Northeast Asian cyber-espionage is escalating in sophistication rather than volume — North Korea's pivot to AI-deepfake-enabled spear-phishing against South Korean military targets, combined with a major diplomatic-database breach in Seoul, shows Pyongyang deepening cyber tradecraft even as it hardens its nuclear-state rhetoric diplomatically.

Two of the region's active ceasefires remain structurally fragile in opposite directions — Thailand and Cambodia are trading violation accusations within days of a Malaysian-brokered truce, while Myanmar's junta shows no ceasefire dynamic at all, broadening its bombing campaign geographically ahead of planned elections.

Democratic processes across South and Southeast Asia remain contested by design — Pakistan's AJK election enters its most volatile phase with a 2 August vote in refugee-seat constituencies, Bangladesh's ruling coalition fractures over its own reform charter, and Indonesia faces mounting scrutiny over shrinking civic space in Papua.

countries.name: North Korea
incidents: 19 Jul — Kaesong vicinity: Satellite imagery confirmed a North Korean base with structures assessed as multiple-rocket-launcher storage facilities.

27 Jul — Pyongyang: Kim Yo Jong rejected the ASEAN Regional Forum's denuclearization call, vowing nuclear capability will be 'continuously upgraded' and calling the DPRK's nuclear-state status 'final and irreversible.'
31 Jul — Seoul: South Korea, the US and nine other countries issued a joint alert on North Korean IT-worker schemes funding weapons programs.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. No kinetic escalation this week, but the armistice-anniversary parade, hardened denuclearization rejection, and continued IT-worker/cyber revenue schemes sustain a consistent high-threat posture. Expect continued rhetorical entrenchment of nuclear-state status while Pyongyang leans on IT-worker and cyber-crime revenue to offset sanctions; a discrete provocation remains plausible within 30-60 days, timed to US-ROK exercises or diplomatic milestones.

countries.name: Myanmar
incidents: 19 Jul — Ma-Ei, Taungup Township, Rakhine: A junta jet dropped three 500-lb bombs, killing 5 civilians.
23 Jul — Kawkareik Township, Karen State: Air and artillery strikes killed at least 10 civilians and displaced thousands.
25-26 Jul — Rakhine/Mandalay/Sagaing: A coordinated wave of airstrikes and drone attacks killed at least 6 civilians, injured 26+, and destroyed 25+ homes and a church.
28 Jul — Wetlet Township, Sagaing Region: Junta airstrikes killed 2 civilians and destroyed roughly 20 homes.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. The bombing campaign has broadened geographically across Rakhine, Mandalay, Sagaing and Karen in a single week, consistent with 450+ civilian deaths from mass-casualty incidents in H1 2026. Expect the junta to sustain or intensify multi-front airstrikes through the election period as a coercive tool against resistance-held territory, with civilian infrastructure remaining at elevated risk and no credible de-escalation signal present.

countries.name: Pakistan
incidents: 27-28 Jul — Rawalakot, AJK: Phase-1 AJK polling was marred by deadly clashes between security forces and JAAC supporters; 2 security personnel and up to 30 protesters were killed over two days.
16 Jul — Balochistan: Operation Shaban's toll reached 129 militants killed since 5 Jul.

31 Jul — AJK-wide: Campaign for phase-2 polling closed, with over 1.7 million voters registered across 21 constituencies including refugee seats — the constituencies most likely to reproduce phase-1 violence given the core grievance over refugee-seat voting rights.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. With phase-2 AJK polling (2 Aug) imminent in the very constituencies where the refugee-seat legitimacy grievance is concentrated, risk of a repeat of the roughly 30-dead phase-1 unrest is elevated. Anticipate a contested and potentially violent phase-2 vote followed by a third phase on 10 Aug, with security forces likely again facing allegations of excessive force; Operation Shaban continues grinding through August without a clear end-state.

countries.name: India
incidents: 21 Jul — Chandel/Ukhrul districts, Manipur: Security forces arrested 3 KYKL cadres and destroyed 2 illegal insurgent bunkers.

28-29 Jul — Imphal West/East, Tengnoupal, Kakching, Manipur: Six militants from KCP, PLA/RPF and SOREPA were arrested in coordinated operations with a large arms and explosives cache seized; a suspect was separately arrested for a grenade attack in Singjamei.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. Manipur counter-insurgency operations continue at a steady tempo along the porous Indo-Myanmar border corridor, with periodic arrests and arms seizures. No indicators of a broadening conflict or major flare-up were found for this period.

countries.name: China
incidents: 20-21 Jul — Taiwan Strait: A PLA helicopter and UAV crossed the median line together and lingered east of it for roughly 9.5 hours.
20 & 24 Jul — Second Thomas Shoal/Scarborough Shoal: Chinese Coast Guard personnel rammed and clashed with Philippine Navy craft and used water cannon against resupply vessels.

26 Jul — Beijing: The PLA Southern Theater Command publicly accused the Philippines of 'stirring up trouble' in the South China Sea, conducting patrols concurrent with a US-Japan-Philippines exercise.

27-28 Jul — South China Sea: The USS George Washington carrier strike group entered the South China Sea in direct response to the Scarborough/Second Thomas Shoal clashes, prompting sharp Chinese rhetoric.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. Beijing is combining rhetorical escalation, gray-zone survey activity, and coast guard pressure without kinetic escalation against a now-present US carrier group. Expect continued PRC gray-zone survey and patrol activity east of Taiwan and around Scarborough/Second Thomas Shoal, calibrated to avoid direct confrontation with the US carrier presence while maintaining pressure on Philippine resupply missions.

countries.name: Taiwan
incidents: 9-29 Jul — Islandwide: The Han Kuang 41 exercise, the largest and longest in the program's history, ran its full 10-day course.

24 Jul — Keelung: Prosecutors detained an Nvidia employee, expanding the AI-chip smuggling probe to 7 suspects, including two from Super Micro and one from Albatron Technology, over forged documents used to ship roughly 50 servers worth NT$700M to China.
31 Jul — Waters east of Taiwan: Confirmed continuous PRC Coast Guard presence and repeated 'marine survey' activity since June, assessed as jurisdiction-building gray-zone activity.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. No new median-line crossing incidents were reported this week, with PLA activity assessed as reverting toward a pre-2024 baseline, but the expanding chip-smuggling probe and sustained gray-zone presence justify maintaining HIGH. Expect the investigation to expand further, potentially implicating additional companies and testing Taiwan-US technology security cooperation, while PRC gray-zone presence east of Taiwan persists.

countries.name: Philippines
incidents: 20 Jul — Second Thomas Shoal: China Coast Guard personnel rammed a Philippine inflatable craft and exchanged blows, injuring a service member; the US formally condemned the incident.
21-25 Jul — South China Sea: The Philippines conducted the 17th Multilateral Maritime Cooperative Activity, a five-day joint exercise with the US and Japan.

24 Jul — Scarborough Shoal: China Coast Guard used water cannon and blocking maneuvers to prevent a Philippine fishermen resupply mission; the previously reported floating Chinese structure at the shoal has since been removed.

27-28 Jul — South China Sea: The USS George Washington carrier strike group, with escort vessels, entered the South China Sea, explicitly framed by the US ambassador as upholding freedom of navigation.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. Direct physical confrontation frequency has plateaued since the 20-24 July clashes, but the deployment of a full US carrier strike group marks a new plateau of great-power military presence around the dispute. Expect the CSG's presence to persist as a deterrence signal through August, raising the risk of a miscalculation incident, with further Philippine resupply missions remaining likely flashpoints.

countries.name: South Korea
incidents: 23 Jul — Seoul: A significant data breach at a government-run diplomatic training academy potentially compromised the personal data of nearly all South Korean diplomats.
Late Jul — Nationwide: A Unification Ministry-run North Korean defector aid organization recorded 944 cyberattack attempts between January and 15 July 2026.
Late Jul — South Korea: Kimsuky attempted a spear-phishing attack on a military-related organization using an AI-generated deepfake military ID image disguised as ID-issuance correspondence.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. The diplomat database breach and AI-deepfake-enabled spear-phishing represent a meaningful escalation in sophistication and target sensitivity beyond the previously known groupware compromise. Expect continued North Korean state-linked cyber operations against South Korean government, defense and NGO targets, increasingly employing generative-AI tradecraft, with further public advisories likely.

countries.name: Vietnam
incidents: 26-27 Jul — near Fiery Cross/Yongshu Reef, Chinese-occupied waters: The Vietnamese cargo ship Khoi Nguyen 18, carrying 62 people, sank in bad weather with 17 crew reported missing; six Chinese vessels and a rescue helicopter assisted alongside one Vietnamese vessel, and Vietnam's Foreign Ministry publicly thanked China for its assistance.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. This was a maritime-safety incident rather than a security escalation, notable for occurring near a Chinese-occupied feature and prompting unusually cooperative Vietnam-China search-and-rescue coordination. Expect Vietnam to continue avoiding overt bloc-alignment, as with its non-signature of the Hague Tribunal anniversary statement, while quietly deepening functional cooperation with China where convenient.

countries.name: Japan
incidents: 19-23 Jul — Tokyo: Defense Minister Koizumi's remarks that Japan 'cannot avoid' a nuclear-weapons debate continued to draw sustained coverage.
Late Jul — Tokyo: Japan is reportedly developing its own central intelligence agency for the first time since WWII, alongside defense reforms loosening arms-export restrictions.
Late Jul — Tokyo/Canberra: Japan agreed to sell Mogami-class frigates to Australia and is discussing a similar sale with New Zealand.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained, watch for upgrade. These are structural and policy developments rather than kinetic ones, continuing the trajectory begun by Koizumi's nuclear-debate remarks. Expect continued PRC pushback against Japan's defense normalization alongside deepening Japan-Australia-Philippines-South Korea security cooperation, though an actual policy shift remains unlikely within the 90-day window.

countries.name: Indonesia
incidents: 17 Jul — KM 4 Logpon area, Dekai District, Yahukimo: Indonesian security forces killed 3 TPNPB-OPM members.

20-21 Jul — Seradala District, Yahukimo: TPNPB-OPM executed 3 civilians accused of acting as informants; the body of the third victim was recovered from the Kolof River on 30 Jul, confirming the full toll.

30 Jul — Papua: HRW published 'Grabbed Land, Silenced Justice,' documenting alleged suppression of environmental activists and journalists in South Papua amid militarization tied to development projects.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. Confirmation of the full civilian death toll from the Yahukimo killings, plus a critical HRW report on shrinking civic space, sustain elevated concern despite no new kinetic clash this week. Expect continued low-intensity TPNPB-OPM activity met by Indonesian security operations, with international human-rights scrutiny likely to intensify following the HRW report.

countries.name: Thailand
incidents: 24 Jul — Thai-Cambodia border: Deadly fighting killed at least 38 and displaced roughly 300,000 on both sides.
28 Jul — Kuala Lumpur: A new unconditional ceasefire was brokered by PM Anwar Ibrahim between Thai Acting PM Phumtham and Cambodian PM Hun Manet.

29-30 Jul — Sisaket province border: Thailand accused Cambodian forces of small-arms and grenade attacks hours after the ceasefire took effect, escalating to a 'flagrant violation' accusation; Cambodia denied responsibility.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. The ceasefire is holding at a strategic level, with no return to large-scale combat, but remains fragile with recurring mutual violation accusations around Sisaket, consistent with last week's assessment. Expect continued Malaysian-mediated engagement, but durable de-escalation and repatriation of the 300,000 displaced is unlikely within 90 days absent a more formalized border-demarcation mechanism.

countries.name: Bangladesh
incidents: 20 Jul — Dhaka: BNP Chairperson Tarique Rahman held his first formal meeting with alliance-party leaders, discussing coordination and implementation of movement-era commitments.

22 Jul — Dhaka: The BNP publicly distanced itself from the July National Charter-backed reform agenda, favoring its own 31-point outline; Jamaat-e-Islami and the NCP criticized the move as contradicting the 2024 July Uprising's spirit.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. The BNP-NCP/Jamaat rift over implementation mechanics has hardened into explicit public divergence, raising the risk of a genuine constitutional impasse ahead of the national election. Expect continued political friction and possible parliamentary gridlock, with risk of street mobilization by NCP/Jamaat-aligned groups if BNP is seen as backsliding.

countries.name: Sri Lanka
incidents: 5-6 Jul — Negombo Prison: The Human Rights Commission confirmed the prison violence left at least 28 dead, including 7 prison officials.
7-8 Jul — Welikada Prison: HRCSL officers were initially denied access during an unannounced inspection visit.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. No new verifiable security incidents were found this week; the Negombo/Welikada prison investigation continues without a confirmed public update. Expect HRCSL and the government's three-member committee to continue investigating without near-term published findings; watch for renewed unrest if investigation delays or torture allegations regarding transferred inmates become public.

regions.name: Americas
overview: Washington's direct hand in hemispheric transitions is deepening on multiple fronts — brokering a new round of Venezuela dialogue between rival National Assemblies, signaling an intensified security partnership with Peru's new government, and an Ecuador partnership HRW says is proliferating torture — showing US-backed militarized security doctrine spreading across the Andean-Caribbean corridor even as it draws mounting rights scrutiny.

Electoral and institutional transitions are fraying under contested-legitimacy pressure rather than being resolved by results — Colombia's 7 August inauguration proceeds under an 11,000-strong security lockdown with the transition itself suspended amid unproven fraud claims, while Bolivia's arrest order against Evo Morales risks reigniting the 53-day blockade crisis it seeks to punish.

Political violence is clustering around succession and transition windows — the Cúcuta truck bombing days before Colombia's inauguration, the unresolved killings of investigators probing Ecuador's president and US military operations, and Haiti's gang expansion into ungoverned territory all point to armed actors exploiting governance vacuums when state authority is in flux.

State capacity to hold territory remains the region's binding constraint on stability — Haiti's Gang Suppression Force still fields under a fifth of its authorized strength against gangs holding roughly 85% of the capital, Cuba's grid and economy keep deteriorating under sanctions pressure, and comparatively stable states like the Dominican Republic and Jamaica continue absorbing spillover from less stable neighbors.

countries.name: Venezuela
incidents: 28 Jul — Caracas: Machado-aligned opposition supporters marched demanding release of political prisoner Gabriel Barros, while a simultaneous Chavista counter-mobilization denounced perceived US influence.

30 Jul — Aboard Air Force One: Trump said Acting President Delcy Rodríguez 'probably has to say' Maduro remains the legitimate president, after Rodríguez called Maduro 'the legitimate president' in an NBC interview from Caracas.

31 Jul-1 Aug — Caracas: US-backed talks opened between Venezuela's two rival National Assemblies, aimed at an electoral-reform roadmap; Machado, excluded from the talks, said she would not obstruct 'real progress' but would judge success by institution restoration, prisoner releases and a real election date.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. The new dialogue track is a potentially positive development, but four prior rounds (2017-2024) collapsed, Machado's faction is excluded, and the Trump administration's direct brokering role underscores how unsettled sovereignty and legitimacy questions remain. Expect Rodríguez's caretaker authority to stay internationally contested but domestically unchallenged, with risk of renewed street mobilization from either faction if the talks are seen as excluding Machado or yield no concrete election date.

countries.name: Haiti
incidents: 20 Jul — New York (UNSC): GSF Special Representative Jack Christofides presented the force's first detailed operational roadmap and formally requested a mandate extension through September 2028.
Ongoing — Port-au-Prince: The GSF remains at roughly 1,000 of 5,550 authorized personnel; full operational capacity is not expected until October 2026.

Ongoing — H1 2026 tally: OHCHR recorded at least 2,310 deaths, 99 kidnappings and 699 sexual-violence victims nationwide, underscoring the scale of the crisis even absent a single new dated incident this week.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. No new dated attack was independently confirmed this week, but the GSF will likely remain understrength through the reporting period, reaching only partial operational capacity by October, meaning no material reduction in gang territorial control is expected before year-end. The mandate-extension request through September 2028 signals the mission itself now expects a multi-year resolution; displacement pressure into Artibonite, Centre and Kenscoff will likely continue.

countries.name: Colombia
incidents: 28-29 Jul — Bogotá: President-elect de la Espriella suspended the administrative transition process after Petro alleged an '848,000-vote fraud' involving Israeli firm Black Cube; Colombia's Inspector General and international observers found no evidence of fraud.

31 Jul — Cali: Security ministry confirmed deployment of 11,000+ soldiers and police for the 7 Aug inauguration, with anti-explosive units, air support, a drone ban and a proposed citywide alcohol ban from 6 Aug.

1 Aug — Cúcuta: A truck bomb detonated beside the police command post, injuring at least 11 (8 police, 3 civilians), six days before the inauguration; officials called it a 'cowardly terrorist attack.'
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained, trending toward the top of the band. The Cúcuta bombing is the first mass-casualty attack directly tied to inauguration week, layered on top of a suspended institutional transition. Expect further attacks on security infrastructure through and past 7 Aug, concentrated in Cúcuta/Norte de Santander and Cali/Valle del Cauca, with the Petro-de la Espriella standoff carrying continued risk of a broader legitimacy dispute; ELN/Clan del Golfo violence in Chocó continues unabated, insulated from Bogotá's political turmoil.

countries.name: Cuba
incidents: 24 Jul — Havana/Santiago de Cuba/Cienfuegos: Cacerolazo protests occurred despite pre-emptive power restorations ahead of the 26 Jul Revolution Day anniversary.
26 Jul — Nationwide: Grid deficit exceeded 2,200 MW on Revolution Day itself, with outages affecting all provinces amid fuel reserves exhausted since May.
30 Jul — Havana: President Díaz-Canel dismissed a US State Department report on Cuba as a 'propaganda pamphlet,' redirecting blame for blackout-driven unrest onto Washington.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. No new dated incident was confirmed beyond the Revolution Day period, but this remains the largest sustained protest wave since July 2021 and still spreading geographically. The regime's tactic of selectively restoring power to defuse planned protest dates has proven only partially effective; expect continued near-daily localized cacerolazos through August as fuel shortages persist, with Díaz-Canel's rhetorical strategy of externalizing blame onto the US likely to continue.

countries.name: Ecuador
incidents: 21 Jul — Manabí/Sucumbíos: HRW's 'A Dangerous Partnership' report documented a March 2026 joint US-Ecuador operation in which soldiers tortured four Colombian dairy workers, released them without charge, then bombed their farm.

29 Jul — Montañita/Manta: Renewed scrutiny surfaced around two unresolved June killings — Mónika Silva Koniuszek, who had been investigating alleged cocaine-trafficking ties to the Noboa family's banana business, and Gloria Alexandra Bravo Cedeño, a prosecutor investigating US drone strikes on Ecuadorian fishing vessels; no arrests have been made in either case.
Ongoing — 10 provinces: A 60-day state of emergency remains in effect, with 879 homicides recorded in emergency zones over a 6-week span.
countries.coa: Upgraded to CRITICAL from HIGH. The convergence of documented state-sanctioned torture in US-partnered operations, unresolved killings of people investigating the president's family and US military operations, and Ecuador's new 'high risk' classification in the Global Torture Index represents a qualitative escalation beyond routine cartel-violence reporting. Expect continued emergency-power renewals, growing HRW/UN/Congressional scrutiny of US-Ecuador security cooperation, and risk of further targeted killings tied to Noboa-family or US-operation investigations.

countries.name: Peru
incidents: 28 Jul — Lima: Keiko Fujimori was inaugurated in the new bicameral Congress; opposition legislators held up photos of 2022-2023 protest victims and walked out during her 'iron fist' security speech.
30 Jul — Lima: Fujimori's cabinet sought congressional approval for a citizen-security package and requested delegated legislative powers to govern by emergency decree.
31 Jul — Lima: Fujimori signaled intent to deepen a 'strategic partner' security relationship with the Trump administration.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. The delegated-powers request and immediate opposition backlash indicate the new administration's emergency-rule approach is already contested. Watch for the first invocations of emergency decree authority, reactivation of 2022-2023-linked protest networks, and expanding US security cooperation potentially including extraditions and military deployments to crime zones.

countries.name: Bolivia
incidents: 29 Jul — La Paz/Washington: The IMF and Bolivia reached agreement on a $1.9 billion financing program, pending board approval.
30 Jul — Santa Cruz: Departmental prosecutors issued an arrest order against Evo Morales over the May-June road blockades, citing armed uprising, terrorism and other charges.

Ongoing — Chapare: Morales remains sheltered by supporters, calling the charges a 'brutal judicial war'; loyalists describe being ready to reinstate blockades at a moment's notice, and Chapare has experienced power outages Morales attributes to government retaliation.
countries.coa: Upgraded to HIGH from MODERATE. The arrest order directly threatens to reignite the blockade crisis that paralyzed the country for 53 days; Morales loyalists' explicit readiness to remobilize is a concrete near-term flashpoint the prior rating understated. Expect a high risk of renewed Chapare/Cochabamba road blockades if security forces attempt to serve the warrant, with echoes possible of the Nov 2024 hostage-taking of soldiers; the IMF financing may stabilize macro conditions but is unlikely to defuse the political standoff.

countries.name: Dominican Republic
incidents: 30 Jul — Santo Domingo: The 2026 deportation campaign reached 226,500 Haitians deported year-to-date, at a pace of roughly 1,000 per day.
countries.coa: LOW maintained. No new security-specific incident was found this week; the deportation campaign continues at its established pace. No security escalation indicators were identified for the period.

countries.name: Jamaica
incidents: 24 Jul — Spanish Town: INDECOM opened a probe into a fatal police shooting on St John's Road.
26 Jul — Mandeville: A shootout on Caledonia Road left three dead; two firearms were recovered.
26 Jul — West Kingston: A fatal police shooting followed a stolen-vehicle pursuit on Spanish Town Road.
30 Jul — Harbour View, Kingston: One man was killed and a firearm seized in a police shootout.
countries.coa: LOW maintained. The broader trend of declining fatal police shootings (8 in July through the 21st versus 20 in June) continues to hold despite several discrete violent incidents in the final week of July. Community-protest risk over police lethality remains latent but not currently active.
